question: Does the existing surface-plus-quadratic-tilt predictor outperform standard interpolation under the same buffered quarter-eye holdouts?
status: Follow-up control on previously examined specimens; specified before calculating these comparator errors, not a preregistered independent validation.

unchanged.input_coordinates: First two surface PCA coordinates, centred at surface medians and divided by surface standard deviations.
unchanged.primary_metric: Median unsigned manual-reference axis error in degrees, reported separately per eye.
unchanged.reference_targets: Leading PCA axes of the same manual voxel clouds.
unchanged.site_correspondence: Nearest corneal point to each supplied cone centre.

symmetric_inputs: Apply both interpolators to outward-oriented unit axes directly and to axis-minus-surface-normal residuals. Add the query surface normal only for the residual versions. Normalise predictions before scoring.
duplicate_sites: After each training split, average vectors at exactly identical standardised surface sites. Do not renormalise averaged training targets; normalise final predictions.
reporting: Keep both fixed comparator settings and every specimen/fold, including large errors and failures. No settings selected using target errors; no inferential statistics treating cones as independent eyes.
verification: Original four methods must reproduce every saved per-cone error and fold assignment within 1e-7 degrees; abort otherwise.
interpretation: These are comparator checks within three previously seen eyes, not biological uncertainty calibration, new specimen replication, complete lens reconstruction or fossil validation.
